## This run specifically

Fix GitHub issue #52 in the UsageFoundry repository (Xapicc/UsageFoundry): https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/52 — "A midnight schedule in a zone that shifts at midnight skips a local day — and a weekly Sunday schedule fires on Saturday". Read the full issue body with `gh issue view 52` first; it contains measured output, the reason the direction flips, and the fix.

The fault: `zonedTime` in `src/lib/schedules.ts` (~265-275) resolves a local wall time in two offset passes. For a zone whose spring-forward transition falls at local midnight (America/Santiago, America/Havana), a nominal time inside the skipped hour lands on the *previous local date* — so one local day gets no occurrence, the day before gets two, and a weekly Sunday schedule fires on Saturday while `describeSchedule` still renders "Every Sunday at 00:00". Europe/Berlin works only because its transition sits at 01:00Z and the correction happens to go forward; `schedules.test.ts:109` pins the invariant against that one zone, which is why the suite is green.

The fix: both candidate instants are already computed inside `zonedTime` (`wall - zoneOffset(wall, tz)` and `wall - zoneOffset(first, tz)`). The property to hold is that the result renders back on the local date it was asked for — check it with `zonedParts`, prefer the candidate that satisfies it, and fall back to the transition instant when the nominal time genuinely does not exist. This must preserve the existing Europe/Berlin behaviour (both candidates are on the requested day there; take the one at-or-after the nominal time) and must not disturb `MAX_DAYS_AHEAD`, which already re-enters correctly because the returned instant is strictly greater than `after`.

Regression tests: extend `nextOccurrence across a DST boundary` in `src/lib/schedules.test.ts` with America/Santiago and America/Havana (both in the tzdata Node ships), covering daily 00:00, daily 00:30 and the weekly-Sunday case — the weekday one is the assertion that reads wrong at a glance. Assert each local day gets exactly one occurrence across the transition.

Out of scope: `everyHours` is an interval off an anchor and is DST-immune by construction — leave it. Fall-back (autumn) behaviour is correct and covered at `schedules.test.ts:136` — do not change it.

Done looks like: `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` both pass (run them; report the real output), the new cases fail before your change and pass after, the work is committed to your own branch, and issue #52 is closed on GitHub with a comment saying what you changed, which files, how you tested it, and naming your branch (`git branch --show-current`) since the fix is not landed yet. Use `gh issue close 52 --comment "…"`.

Practical notes: you are working in an isolated git worktree, so `node_modules` may be absent — run `npm install` first if it is. Commit as you go. Do not push, do not open a pull request; the operator lands the branch. Do not edit CLAUDE.md or README.md: several runs are working this repository in parallel and those two files are shared conflict surface, and this fix restores documented behaviour rather than changing an invariant.

If — and only if — this cannot be resolved without a decision only a human can make, then as an absolute last resort: make no changes at all, run `git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -fd` so your branch carries no commits and the tree is clean, post a comment on issue #52 explaining exactly what decision is needed and why you stopped, do NOT close the issue, and finish. The issue spells out a fix direction, so prefer the smallest change that satisfies it.
